canonScope.foundation: Steins;Gate visual novel continuity and terminology, with later Steins;Gate/Steins;Gate 0 material explicitly named when used.
canonScope.variantPolicy: World lines, attractor fields, adaptations, side games and later Science Adventure appearances remain labelled rather than merged.

entities.name: Rintaro Okabe
entities.summary: Founder of the Future Gadget Laboratory and primary witness to world-line changes through Reading Steiner.

entities.name: Kurisu Makise
entities.summary: Neuroscientist and Lab Member 004; central to the Time Leap Machine, the Alpha/Beta divergence crisis, and Operation Skuld.

entities.name: Mayuri Shiina
entities.summary: Okabe's childhood friend and Lab Member 002; her repeated death is a major Alpha-attractor convergence point.

entities.name: Itaru Hashida
entities.summary: Lab Member 003 and expert hacker/engineer; co-creator of the PhoneWave and a key future time-machine builder.

entities.name: Suzuha Amane
entities.summary: Time traveller and Lab Member 008 whose missions differ by attractor field and who guides Okabe toward Steins Gate.

entities.name: Future Gadget Laboratory
entities.summary: Akihabara maker-space and social group founded in March 2010; its inventions and relationships jointly drive the causal structure of the story.

rules.name: World Line
rules.summary: A complete self-consistent history. Many possible world lines exist, but only one is physically active at a time.

rules.name: Active World Line
rules.summary: The physically realised history. When the active line changes, history and ordinary memory reconstruct to match the newly active line.

rules.name: Divergence
rules.summary: A numeric identifier/difference measure for world lines, displayed by the Divergence Meter.

rules.name: Attractor Field
rules.summary: A bundle of world lines with shared convergence outcomes despite local variation.

rules.name: World Line Convergence
rules.summary: Within an attractor field, local interventions may alter how an event occurs while the field still converges on the same outcome.

rules.name: Reading Steiner
rules.summary: Okabe's anomalous preservation of memories across world-line shifts. Other people can retain weaker echoes as dreams or déjà vu.

attractorFields.convergence: World War III over time-travel research
avoids principal Alpha and Beta terminal outcomes

technologies.name: PhoneWave (name subject to change)
technologies.summary: Future Gadget No. 8; accidentally becomes capable of sending short messages to the past and forms the basis of later time-leap work.

technologies.name: D-Mail
technologies.summary: A short message sent to the past; if its effects contradict prior history it can activate a different world line.

technologies.name: Time Leap Machine
technologies.summary: Transmits a person's memory data to their own earlier brain. The standard Alpha-era safe jump is 48 hours; later implementations extend the interval.

technologies.name: Divergence Meter
technologies.summary: A future Okabe instrument used with Reading Steiner to quantify/identify world-line changes.

technologies.name: Amadeus System
technologies.summary: An AI system built from digitised human memory and personality data; Amadeus Kurisu is central in Steins;Gate 0.

events.name: First D-Mail / initial world-line shift
events.summary: Okabe's message about Kurisu's apparent death is received in the past, beginning the principal sequence of world-line changes.

events.name: Mayuri convergence loop
events.summary: Repeated time leaps alter circumstances but not Mayuri's Alpha-field death, demonstrating convergence.

events.name: Operation Skuld
events.summary: The plan to reach Steins Gate by preserving the observation that motivates past Okabe while changing the causal facts that would lead to Kurisu's death and the Beta-field war.

revisionNotes: World lines are not collapsed into parallel simultaneously physical worlds in this package; the active/inactive distinction is preserved.
Adaptation and side-continuity material stays labelled.
No source prose is mirrored wholesale; records are compact paraphrased canon/index data.
